relevance_note: The paper reports three probands with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants: 'Here we describe three unrelated patients with autoimmune lupus nephritis (LN) phenotypes carrying three novel mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene.'
method_note: Read the full paper and built the JSON with a Python script (scratch build.py) whose values I typed from my reading; Table 5 (common SLE risk variants) rows were transcribed by script from the Markdown lines and checked cell by cell against the table. All spans were verified verbatim by script. Tables 1-3 have patients as columns; column headers are 'Patient 1 | Patient 2 | Patient 3' (text uses P1/P2/P3); labels 'Patient 1/2/3' are used throughout. Table 4 and Table 5 continuation rows have a blank patient cell; they were attributed to the patient on the preceding labelled row (the converter did not repeat these labels). Relatives: P1's mother (recurrent oral ulcers; carrier inferred only from Table 1 'Mutation origin | From mother'), P1's son (clinical features; no explicit genotype - the paper only says the mutation 'co-segregated with disease phenotype in the family', so no variant row), P3's mother (asymptomatic carrier, Sanger-confirmed), and P2's two parents (tested negative: 'neither parent harboured the variant'); the paper gives no individual labels for P2's parents, so 'P2’s parent (1)/(2)' are constructed labels with sex not reported. P3's father underwent trio WES but no result is stated, so he has no row. For P3's mother, 'asymptomatic' is recorded as one phenotypic_features row with status 'excluded' (meaning symptoms reported absent); her checklist is left 'not reported' because 'asymptomatic' is not feature-specific. age_at_diagnosis_original_text gives both LN and genetic diagnosis ages; age_at_diagnosis_iso8601 uses the LN (clinical) diagnosis age. Table 5 zygosity was read from the GT column (0/1 or 0|1 = heterozygous, 1/1 or 1|1 = homozygous); the chrX CXorf21 call in the male P1 (GT 1/1) is left 'not reported'. Table 5 variant_type left 'not reported' (authors give location, not class); for non-coding rows without a consequence string the rsID is the variant string. Checklist judgments: P1 thrombocytopenia not marked as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' because autoimmune cause is not stated; P3 'Bilateral knee effusion' marked as arthritis or arthralgia observed; P2 'vasculitic rashes' marked vasculitis observed; P1's son Henoch–Schönlein purpura marked vasculitis observed; Table 1 'Musculoskeletal: No' and 'Ocular: No' used to exclude arthritis/arthralgia and ocular inflammation for P2 (and ocular for P3). P2 had no autoantibodies during the first year then developed ANA (temporal, not contradictory). P3 had fever before treatment and 'no fever' during follow-up (treatment outcome, recorded as detail, not as an excluded row). Minor inconsistencies in the paper: P2 treatment text says 'methylprednisolone with cyclosporine' while Table 4 says 'P + cyclosporine A' (P = prednisone); P2 immunofluorescence text omits C9 listed in Table 2; P1 extraglomerular deposits text lists IgG, IgA and C1q while Fig. 1 legend mentions IgG and IgA; Discussion says P2 and P3 had marked autoimmunity '<3 year' whereas Table 1 gives LN diagnosis at 3 years. Discussion statements pooled across the three patients ('They shared ... recurrent oral ulcers, intermittent fever ...') were not used for per-person status. No ethnicity, consanguinity or vital status is stated for any person.
